_comment: 1959 - one window. Left: the die's membrane through a 1 kHz DC-coupled ADC, drawn as the installation's spiral. Right: the Hubel & Wiesel film, whose soundtrack is what stimulates the die. Shared keys are parsed by ../../ofxLPM/coro/src/Settings.h; the keys below the divider are this app's own.
_splitFraction: Fraction of the window width given to the membrane. The rest is the film, letterboxed on black - the film is the evidence, so none of it is cropped.
_spiral: theta = 2*pi*(t mod spiralPeriod)/spiralPeriod, r = radiusBase + radiusGain*warp(V). Radii are fractions of half the SHORT edge of the LEFT panel, so a half-width panel on a 16:9 screen is square and the spiral fills it.
_radiusBase: Keep radiusBase above radiusGain. Otherwise a deep reset drives the radius through zero and every notch collapses onto one hot point at the centre instead of drawing its shape.
_radiusGamma: Signed power law on the radius. Below 1 lifts the small signal, which is right when the subthreshold dynamics survive the input path - and on a DC-coupled ADC they do.
_radiusMin: Inner floor as a fraction of half the short edge. The crash carries V past -1, so without a floor every reset collapses onto one point at the centre; this is the ring the notches bottom out on.
_drawDuck: Collapse the drawn radius toward the base ring except around a DETECTED spike. Off here: on a DC-coupled path there is real structure between spikes and it is worth seeing.
_traceAlphaQuiet: Brightness between spikes, absolute alpha. Ring equilibrium is roughly (samplesPerRevolution / ringPerimeterPx) * revsPerSec * alpha * decaySeconds, so it scales inversely with deviceRateHz: 0.12 at 400 Hz becomes 0.048 at 1 kHz. Rescale it if you change deviceRateHz or spiralPeriod.
_persistence: Old trajectory decays exponentially over decaySeconds; the buffer is never cleared. Lower it for a faster fade - but raise traceAlphaQuiet in proportion or the base ring dims with it.
_scope: Live monitor of the raw volts along the bottom of the LEFT panel, with its own manual gain - deliberately not the level-normalised signal the spiral uses, so it stays an honest picture of what is arriving. Set scopePanel false for the spiral alone.
_membraneDetector: Detection on the reset edge of the die's membrane, at the BOARD's rate. Tuned against a 400 Hz scope capture of the same pin (ofxLPM/scopeanalogpin/ucope_33.csv): rest 279 mV, staircase to threshold 1050 mV over ~12.5 ms, crash of -643 mV in one sample, recovery over ~20 ms. followerFallMs is a time, so it does not need rescaling with the sample rate - it wants to be longer than the crash and shorter than the recovery.
_audio: 1959 in the left ear, 2026 in the right. Left is the film's own soundtrack downmixed to mono; right is a tick struck by each measured reset and decaying. Nothing free-runs: unplug the board (or switch tickSource to aer and unplug the chip) and the right channel goes silent.
_tickGain: Level of the chip's channel relative to the film's, on top of outputGain*mixSpike. The die is one short grain per spike against a continuous soundtrack, so it needs the trim to sit in the same room. This file is re-read within a second of being saved, so it can be set by ear with the piece running; the - and = keys do the same live and log the value to write back here.
_tickSource: Where the right channel's tick comes from. 'membrane' is the analog reset the ADC measured - the physics, and what the spiral is drawing. 'aer' is the chip's own digital report of the same spike over the AER handshake, which keeps the room alive if the ADC board is not connected. 'both' strikes on either.
_film: The film's soundtrack, decoded to interleaved stereo S16LE at sampleRate by ./prepare.sh. It is the master clock: the video is nudged to follow it, never the reverse. The detector runs on its LEFT channel, which is where the electrode is.
_filmDetector: Detection of the cat's clicks on the tape. A clean recording, so the level envelope is off and the threshold is absolute in input units. These are the values ofxLPM/hubel-wiesel-audio-filter settled on.
_chip: The die is brought up in stages once neuron_bridge.py says READY: biases, then monitor, then PROG, then ROUTE, then run. PROG must precede ROUTE - programming a weight re-runs spikesetup on the chip and clobbers whatever route was staged.
_chipEnabled: false runs the picture and the sound with the die untouched: no bridge is spawned, no DAC is written, nothing takes the FTDI. For testing the projection, the film and the speakers without the chip on the plinth - and for leaving the bench free while you do it.
_bridgePath: The FTDI driver, spawned as a child process and spoken to over a pipe. Relative to the executable. tools/ holds a copy taken from the chip's own repository; on that bench, point this at the maintained one (../../neuron_bridge.py there) so there is a single source of truth rather than two that drift.
_chipSynapse: chipSynapse is the synapse that is routed to the neuron and fired. chipProgSyn is a second synapse that is weight-programmed alongside it and otherwise left alone - the bench sequence is written down as PROG S14 while the route that carries the film is S0, so both are given the weight. Set chipProgSyn to -1 to program only the routed one.
_trig: One TRIG per detected click, rate limited on the host. The UART cannot take a burst and a click train is exactly a burst; excess clicks are dropped rather than queued, so the die stays in step with what is on screen instead of falling behind it.
_device: The board streams 'seconds,volts' over USB CDC at deviceRateHz. pixhawk-scope/src/main.c is 1 kHz. The index comes from the sample count, not the timestamp: the board's rate is exact and its timestamp is a display convention that wraps. The app measures the arriving line rate every 5 s and logs a warning if it disagrees with this value by more than 15%.
